scenario: LEXP.7.19: `==` on two `Bytes` values compares their content. Pair p1 holds the same three octets in both slots, so `p.a == p.b` is true and the rule fires. Pair p2 holds two values of one length that differ in the last octet, and p3 a value and a prefix of it; neither fires. Three Pairs plus one Found. A `Bytes` slot is written `{"$bytes": "<hex>"}` (the harness's form, read alike by both drivers). PATH PINNED: a slot-versus-slot test inside one pattern, which no alpha test can carry (there is no `Bytes` literal), so the predicate evaluator answers it: libds `rete/eval.c` `val_eq_unordered` through the BINOP comparison arm; Mercury `ds.eval` `compare_outcome`. p2 pins content over length, p3 length over a shared prefix.
rules_ds:
schema Pair scope logical:
    id: String key
    a: Bytes mutable
    b: Bytes mutable

schema Found scope logical:
    id: String key

rule r:
    Pair p where p.a == p.b
->
    emit Found logical id: p.id
